commentBody: A very clever and well-executed theme. But the fill clues were so easy I wondered why I was bothering to finish the "outer" puzzle before going to the box (reminder: I solve offline). I realize Sunday fill is even easier than it used to be, but when the only challenge was realizing a RESORTarea was really a RESORTTOWN, to me it's a big Monday. Again, I liked the box and the re-clued clues for it. I would have preferred this as a Thursday: less fill and tougher fill clues. YMMV.

First, just a lovely theme idea. How meta, a puzzle within a puzzle. I think it’s a theme that could even be repeated. And think about the difficulty here—it’s not just finding symmetrical clues for another puzzle inside the box—all those clues have to ALSO have a second meaning, the obvious one they were clued as initially, and then another for the inside puzzle. And these were indeed elegant and fun, and didn’t seem forced at all (except maybe GIANT SNOWMAN, and that was too fun to complain about).

Second, I thought this was an appropriate Sunday challenge. I disagree with Barry on this one. Sure not Thursday or Friday level but definitely Wednesday, and I was tricked by a bunch of clues, jumped around a lot, and had a few crannies that looked like they may even defeat me at first. (It would help if I knew the difference between ERES and ESTA and STREUSEL and STREUDEL).

…continued…

King TUT is a great example of how different Polish and (American) English may be. As I've mentioned many times before, Poles shorten words much more rarely than Americans: to us, the young Egyptian ruler is always Tutanchamon (our rendering of Tutankhamun) - a short version of his name simply does not exist in our language. Also, while I suppose it wouldn't literally be wrong to call a pharaoh (faraon) a king (król - the word comes from the name Karol [Wielki], Charlemagne) in Polish, we tend to exclusively use the term "faraon" when talking about any Egyptian ruler of the ancient dynastic era. Thus, your "king TUT" simply doesn't exist in Polish: he's "faraon Tutanchamon" for us, always.

Eventually, FLUTESECTION/STEM came to me, and it was took maybe another 30 seconds from there. But I have to say, I really loved the (completely unexpected) experience of feeling genuinely stumped for those 5 minutes.
